svg.title: Chile wine-growing study atlas
svg.desc: Travel north to south through selected Chilean valleys, distinguishing Pacific-facing sites from inland valleys near the Andes. Approximate study locations, not appellation boundaries. Numbers refer to the study key; a shared number connects places in one grouped lesson. 1: Elqui / Limarí. Two northern valleys; Elqui is north of Limarí. 2: Aconcagua / Casablanca. Inland Aconcagua and coastal Casablanca are distinct wine settings; their shared number preserves the course grouping. 3: Maipo Valley. The central valley around and south of Santiago, with important east–west and elevation differences. 4: Rapel / Colchagua. Rapel encompasses the Cachapoal and Colchagua groupings; Colchagua lies farther south. 5: Curicó / Maule. Neighboring central valleys south of Colchagua; Maule lies south of Curicó. 6: Itata / Bío Bío. Southern wine areas; Itata lies north of Bío Bío.

g.text: Dots locate representative places · boundaries do not represent appellations
